title: Two hundred
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Thursday. The print shop runs two hundred copies of five strips. The tech folds one wrong. Wood keeps the wrong one. The first misprint in the run; he's still got it in 2027.

panels.composition: The college print shop. The machine running. A PRINT TECH in an apron. WOOD watching the copies come out: quarter-letter sheets, five strips each.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a college print shop with a photocopier running and a tech in an apron, a young man watching quarter-letter sheets of comic strips come out

panels.composition: Two hundred, in a stack. The tech folding. One folded backward: the cover inside, the last strip out.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, close-up of a stack of small folded zines with one folded backward so its cover faces inward

panels.composition: The tech reaching to refold it. Wood's hand, first.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a young man taking a misfolded zine from a print tech's hand before it can be refolded

panels.composition: Wood with the misfold in his coat pocket. The stack of a hundred and ninety-nine under his arm. The rack at the laundromat, tomorrow.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a young man leaving a print shop with a stack of zines under his arm and one folded zine tucked into his coat pocket, no words
image.notes: The backward digest: the corkboard inventory should get it (1999, the misfold).

art.line: brush-pen now — the weekday deadline teaches the hand to commit; still xeroxed, still black and white
art.paper: the college paper's newsprint; the digest's quarter-letter xerox
